stage1.impression: This is a tabletop product still of a hammered brass bowl of glossy coloured tokens on a pale, pinkish timber block against a dark wall. It reads as CG. The coins cling to the bowl's sloped inner wall facing the camera, which no gravity would allow. Heavy denoiser smear removes every micro-texture, the wood is a smooth pink procedural with no pores, and the top of the stand is lit almost to paper white while the room around it goes to mud. Nothing places it in a specific bar: there is no door, no concrete, fir or steel, and no EARF speaker, so a magazine would see a generic casino-chip prop shot rather than Planet EARF.

blocking_9: Coins must lie as a gravity-settled heap in the bottom of the bowl (stacked, overlapping, some on edge against the wall), not arranged in a ring stuck to the inner wall facing the lens

The frame must show where it is: the door, the host stand's real material and some of the shell (board-formed concrete, fir, blackened steel, shopfront glass or street light) so the picture reads as Planet EARF and not a tabletop

The stand top must sit at lum_median 90 to 140, not around 200, with a real pool of light falling off across it, and it must read as stained oak or fir with visible grain and pores, not pink-white smooth CG
No clipping in the bowl: the hot spot in the bowl's interior is 30 % clipped and must be under 2 %
Denoiser smear gone: the hammered brass, the coin engraving and the wood grain must hold crisp detail at 1:1 (render at full 2400 x 1600 with more samples, denoise off or at a lower prefilter)
The acrylic coins must read as thick cast acrylic, with polished, glowing edges and some light passing through, not as opaque glossy poker chips with white dashes
Some sign of life and some context in the frame: a hand, a coat, the door's edge, a guest's silhouette beyond

defects.what: Coins float on, or are glued to, the steep inner wall of the bowl in a fan aimed at the camera. Not physically settled.
The bowl's interior hot spot is blown: clip_pct 30.5, lum_p95 254.9
The stand top is overexposed and pink: lum_median 202, RGB 227/197/183, delta-E 29 against a warm oak at #8A6A4E. Smooth procedural streaks, no pores, no wear.
The stand is a plain slab with soft, rounded, blurry edges (an edge width of 54 px at its left edge) and reads as a block of foam or soap, not joinery
Denoiser smear: the hammered brass dimples, the coin engraving and the edges are all mushy, with painterly blotches
The bowl's outer wall reads as flat salmon-pink copper, not brass. It does not match the interior's gold, and its reflections are featureless.
The background is an undifferentiated dark brown wall with faint vertical panels. No concrete texture, no tie holes, nothing identifying the room.
The floor and the right side are murky, low-contrast mud. The shadow shapes are ambiguous.
The coins read as opaque poker or casino chips with white edge dashes. That is the wrong cue for premium acrylic, and their eight saturated tints compete as a confetti of colour.

changes.problem: The coins are arranged on the bowl's steep inner wall facing the lens, which is physically impossible and the single biggest CG tell.

evidence.measured: Seen at 1:1 (crop x2): the coins sit at 30 to 60 degrees on the upper wall with nothing under them

change.setting: props: EARFcoins, the brass bowl of 40 at the door
change.from: coins placed in a ring on the bowl's inner surface
change.to: 40 coins dropped by rigid-body simulation into the bowl so they settle in a heap 2 to 4 deep at the bottom, a few leaning on edge against the wall, and one or two loose on the stand beside the bowl

changes.expected: A believable pile with contact shadows between the coins. Only the top layer's faces are visible and the rest show as edges.

changes.problem: The frame is a tabletop product shot with no sign of the door, the shell or the bar, so it cannot read as a specific place.

out_of_scope.request: Make the coins thick clear-edged cast acrylic with glowing polished edges, and drop the white poker-chip edge dashes
out_of_scope.why: The coins are an EARF product (their tint, design and graphic are fixed by the card). If the dashes are part of the coin design, that is the owner's call, but they read as casino chips.

out_of_scope.request: Limit the bowl to one or two tints rather than all eight
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the bowl as coins in all eight of EARF's tints. This breaks the frame's one-colour rule, which the owner should weigh.

out_of_scope.request: Show an Atmosphere speaker in this frame as the colour hero
out_of_scope.why: Whether the door detail includes a speaker is a framing choice (c2 attempts it). If the door's sightline cannot reach one, the frame cannot satisfy the hero-speaker criterion.
